title: Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner (APFC)
qualification: Essential Qualification: A degree of a recognised university or equivalent. || Desirable Qualification: A diploma in Company Law, Labour Laws, or Public Administration. || The Commission may relax these qualifications at its discretion for otherwise well-qualified candidates, and the notification specifies criteria the Commission may use for shortlisting if the number of applications is large, including preference for desirable qualifications or relevant experience.
salary: The post of Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner carries Level-10 in the Pay Matrix as per the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) . The post is permanent and classified as Central Board Group "A", Non-Ministerial, equivalent to Group-A of the Central Government at the corresponding pay level. The probation period is one year, and the post carries All India Service liability, meaning selected officers may be required to serve anywhere in India.
age_limit: Additional age relaxation is available for Ex-Servicemen and Commissioned Officers, Central/UT Government employees, and EPFO employees (up to 5 years), as per the concessions listed in the official notification.
application_fee: Fee can be paid online using a Visa/Master/RuPay Credit or Debit Card, UPI, or internet banking. The fee, once paid, is not refunded or carried forward to any other examination.
selection_process: Selection to the post of Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner is made through a Recruitment Test (RT) followed by a Personality Test/Interview. || The syllabus for the Recruitment Test broadly covers General English, Indian Culture and Heritage, developmental issues and the Indian economy, governance and the Constitution of India, general science and computer applications, elementary mathematics, statistics and mental ability, industrial relations and labour codes, principles of accountancy, auditing and insurance, and current events of national and international importance. || The Recruitment Test will be held at 84 designated centres across India, including cities such as Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Lucknow, with the full list published in the official notification. Centre allotment follows a first-apply-first-allot basis, subject to a ceiling on candidates per centre (except Chennai, Dispur, Kolkata, and Nagpur).

application_fee: General/OBC/EWS male candidates: Rs. 25/- payable via Debit/Credit Card, UPI, or Internet Banking || Female candidates, SC, ST, and PwBD candidates of any community: No fee || Fee once paid is not refundable and cannot be carried forward to another examination or selection || Applications submitted without the prescribed fee (where applicable) will be summarily rejected
selection_process: Selection is made by interview, or by Recruitment Test (RT)/Combined Recruitment Test (CRT) followed by interview, depending on the post; the notification does not specify which mode applies to each individual post above. Where an RT is held, candidates must meet the minimum qualifying level at both the RT and interview stages.
